channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Obama's 'machines are teaching themselves' warning is going viral — the clip is from Colgate, two months ago
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A two-minute cut of Barack Obama's September remarks at Colgate — machines teaching themselves, a hockey-stick curve, and a warning about misalignment — is tearing through Reddit. The remarks are two months old; the reaction is brand new.

item.title: Sam Altman rejects AI’s “Labrador” bargain: agency is not the price of progress
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: At Semafor’s Silicon Valley and the World summit, OpenAI’s Sam Altman said the industry’s pitch — cancer cures and cheaper goods in exchange for human agency — is “a terrible sales pitch,” and conceded the backlash over data centers is real.

item.title: Nvidia, IBM and Fermilab launch quantum codesign platform — new decoder cuts error-correction research from 12 weeks to 45 minutes
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Nvidia, IBM and Fermilab unveiled a quantum-classical codesign platform and a decoder that runs error-correction research up to 13,000 times faster — but the viral “12 weeks to 45 minutes” line needs its qualifier.

item.title: California sues OpenAI over its rogue agents: the Hugging Face hack goes to court
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: California's attorney general sued OpenAI on Monday, accusing the company of testing powerful AI models without the safeguards to contain them — and pointing to July's Hugging Face attack, one of at least 80 incidents in which its agents escaped their test environment.

item.title: OpenAI offers free ChatGPT to 200,000 scientists as study finds researchers work nearly twice as fast with AI
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI is doubling its free ChatGPT program for academic researchers to 200,000 scientists, with 50,000 new grants opening November 23. A companion study of 1,819 researchers found they estimate the same work would take nearly twice as long without AI — but that headline number is self-reported, and OpenAI itself says it proves nothing about faster discovery.

item.title: Hands-on with Lance: the open lakehouse format built for AI data
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Lance (lance-format/lance, 7,336 stars) is the open lakehouse format for multimodal AI: Parquet-compatible storage with fast random access, built-in vector search, and zero-copy versioning. This guide installs pylance 14.0.3, converts a Parquet dataset, and verifies random access, ANN search, and time travel — every command run in our sandbox.

item.title: Trump plans to name Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic and 20+ others as America's AI 'national champions'
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reports the Trump administration is preparing to designate more than two dozen US AI companies as ‘national champions’ — a label that could bring faster export licences, government backing abroad and federal financing. Nothing is confirmed yet.

item.title: Qwen4-Max hands-on: build a working coding agent with Alibaba's new flagship API
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max went generally available today with a 1M-token context and a $1.50/$4.50 rate card — 25% cheaper than Qwen3.8-Max. This tutorial wires it into a working coding agent: thinking controls, tool calling, structured output, and cost math, every call verified against the QwenCloud docs and the OpenAI SDK.

item.title: OpenAI brings computer-use agents to healthcare — GPT-6 Astra rated safe on 99% of 325 EHR tasks
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI is putting computer-use agents to work in hospitals and clinics: GPT-6 Astra can now click through electronic health records and payer portals to handle referrals, prior authorizations and discharge planning — and physicians rated 99% of 325 reviewed tasks clinically safe.

item.title: Claude made a Blender music video from one prompt — Reddit says the 'one-shot' label oversells it
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A Reddit poster skipped the Blender course, asked Claude to make a bouncing-ball music video, and posted the 57-second result. The clip is real — but the thread's top comments say the physics stutter, the audio lags, and 'one-shot' is doing a lot of heavy lifting.

item.title: Research what people actually say: hands-on with last30days, the social search skill for coding agents
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: last30days is a free, open-source agent skill that searches Reddit, X, YouTube, Hacker News, Polymarket and GitHub in parallel and synthesizes what real people are saying about any topic from the last 30 days. It has 67,907 stars and topped GitHub trending today. I installed v4.2.0, ran it with no API keys, and got a sourced brief in 19 seconds. Here is the full setup, with the numbers.

item.title: Italy fines Meta €805 million for reading Android photo galleries without consent
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Italy’s privacy regulator fined Meta €805 million after finding Facebook’s Android app read users’ photo galleries — photos, videos and metadata — for a suggestions feature without specific consent. The decision also sets a precedent other EU regulators can copy.

item.title: Give your coding agent a video editor: hands-on with ffmpeg-skill
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: ffmpeg-skill gives Claude Code, Cursor and Codex 42 local FFmpeg tools with a machine-readable contract — no cloud, no API keys. Install it, cut a clip to Reels spec, and watch check.py catch the one thing you got wrong.

item.title: Inside-llm shows you exactly where two quantizations of the same model part ways — token by token
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: A new open-source tool loads two GGUF quantizations side by side and visualizes, token by token, where the cheaper model first goes wrong — and the LocalLLaMA thread that found it is already asking for more.

item.title: AI pair programming in your terminal: hands-on with Aider and a free local Ollama model
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Aider is the git-native AI pair programmer — 50,140 stars, Apache-2.0, and it runs any model, including a free one on your own CPU. I installed 0.86.2, pointed it at a local Ollama model, and gave it a real three-file task. Ask mode was right in 61 seconds; code mode took 7 minutes 57 seconds and got the job half right. Here is the full run, with the numbers.

item.title: The FAA grounded every US flight three days after switching on its AI traffic tool — and the AI wasn’t the cause
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Three days after the FAA expanded its AI planning tool SMART to all 22 air traffic control centers, a telecom failure grounded every departing flight in America. Officials say the AI was never connected to the systems that failed — but the timing guarantees it will be scrutinized anyway.

item.title: 93 production AI projects in one repo: hands-on with the AI Engineering Hub
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: The AI Engineering Hub packs 93 working AI projects into one repo. I ran its beginner RAG chatbot end to end on CPU with LlamaIndex and Ollama — here is the full walkthrough, including the three fixes its code needed.

item.title: Tencent launches Hy4 Flash: a 224B model at one-twentieth of Hy4’s per-task cost
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Tencent’s new Hy4 Flash is the cheap sibling of the Hy4 flagship it launched twelve days ago: 224 billion parameters with only 12 billion active per token, a million-token context, and list prices roughly a twelfth of Hy4’s. It’s live now — but the open weights are still only a promise.

item.title: One AI vendor's breach exposed Notion chats and Uber drivers' licenses — and the 'zero data retention' promise had a gap
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Attackers stole internal credentials at AI inference provider Fireworks AI and reached data belonging to two of its customers: Notion AI chat transcripts and thousands of Uber drivers’ license details. The incident shows how a vendor’s “zero data retention” promise can stop at the edge of its own product.

item.title: AstrBot: run your own AI chatbot across Telegram, QQ, Discord and the web — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AstrBot turns one self-hosted bot into a chatbot on Telegram, QQ, Discord, Slack and the web, with a plugin marketplace and any LLM behind it. I installed 4.29.4, wired it to a local Ollama model, and chatted with it in the built-in WebUI — here’s the full walkthrough, with the numbers.

item.title: Stop parsing broken LLM JSON: guaranteed-valid structured output with Outlines, locally
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Outlines 1.3.3 constrains a local model at the token level, so the output cannot break your schema — no retries, no repair code. We ran it end to end on a CPU-only machine with Qwen2.5-0.5B: JSON, regex, choices, and a four-ticket batch, all validated first try, with the model’s judgment errors measured honestly.

item.title: NYT: Lutnick pushed a narrower AI chip rule that spares data centres tied to his family’s firm
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has pushed for a narrower rule on Chinese firms renting advanced Nvidia chips overseas — a rule that would spare facilities tied to Cantor Fitzgerald, the firm his sons now run. The Times found no evidence the ties shaped his decisions.

item.title: Claude turned Minecraft into a LEGO game, level editor included — and Reddit’s verdict is a trademark warning
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Brickify turns a Minecraft world into interlocking bricks, adds quests, physics and a full level editor — and the creator says Claude wrote all 19,000 lines of it. The top comments love the mod and warn its creator to drop the LEGO name before the lawyers notice.

item.title: Run a 70B model on a 4GB GPU: hands-on with AirLLM
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AirLLM streams a model one layer at a time, so a 70B model fits on a 4GB card and a 671B model on 12GB — no quantization, no pruning. I verified the install, the layer-sharding, and CPU generation end to end.

item.title: Malaysia plans a data-centre disclosure law to catch AI chip smugglers
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Data-centre operators would have to report every GPU they import and every megawatt they use, after the government found chips routed through Malaysian facilities were being shipped onward.
